title: tests/fixtures/abi-v1/cases.json, format 1
description: The committed, generated (scripts/abi-v1/emit/cases.py) conformance cases every enrolled binding's v1-abi-conformance leg runs against the stub libraries scripts/abi-v1/build-stubs.sh builds. See that emitter's module docstring for the six case kinds (handshake, echo, status, loader, lifecycle, concurrent) and the argument-expression shapes (int, bytes_hex, handle, null_handle, ref). This schema is checked by scripts/abi-v1/parity.py before it trusts the file, using the same restricted JSON Schema subset spec/abi-v1/abi.json's own schema uses (scripts/abi-v1/model.py's validate()); it is not part of gen.py's abi.json/sdk.json pipeline.

os.description: Present only on a loader case whose expected reason differs by platform (ctor-marker: D3's glibc floor step is Linux-only, so the same library is refused on Linux but accepted on darwin). Absent means the case applies on every platform. A conformance runner must OMIT from its report (never fail, never report a pass for) a case whose os does not match its own platform; the parity gate expects, per leg, only the cases whose os is absent or matches that leg (linux = linux-*, darwin = darwin-*).

steps.description: A lifecycle case's steps, run in order with no other case in flight: `let` binds the handle a call produces to a name a later `ref` argument uses; `call` with `expect` makes a call and checks it as an echo case is checked (every chs_buf it produces freed straight after); `free` releases a bound handle through its own free function; `live_delta` reads chs_live_handles and requires each kind's count to differ from the count read when the case began by exactly the given amount. Every handle a step binds is freed by a step.

threads.description: A concurrent case: how many threads call at once.

calls.description: A concurrent case: how many calls each thread makes.
